title: OOP Design Practice and Review
learningObjectives: Explain oop design practice and review.
Identify relevant class/object relationships and access rules.
Apply the OOP concept in a small design.

understand.concept: Good OOP design gives types cohesive responsibilities, protects invariants and uses composition or inheritance intentionally. Test behavior through the public interface.
understand.whyItMatters: Design practice connects syntax to maintainable software.
understand.explain: Favor small focused classes, predictable ownership and interface-based tests.

examples.title: Focused class
examples.code: class Wallet{public:void add(int amount){if(amount>0)balance+=amount;}int get()const{return balance;}private:int balance=0;};
examples.explanation: Wallet owns one focused responsibility and validates updates.

examples.title: Use composition
examples.code: struct Address{std::string city;};\nstruct Person{std::string name;Address address;};
examples.explanation: Person has an Address; composition expresses ownership/part-of.

examples.title: Interface-based test
examples.code: class Counter{public:void inc(){++n;}int get()const{return n;}private:int n=0;};\nCounter c;c.inc();assert(c.get()==1);

examples.title: Avoid public state
examples.code: class Bank{public:bool deposit(int n){if(n<=0)return false;amount+=n;return true;}private:int amount=0;};

examples.title: Choose composition over inheritance
examples.code: struct Engine{void start(){}};\nstruct Car{Engine engine;void start(){engine.start();}};
examples.explanation: A Car contains an Engine rather than inheriting its identity.

practise.guidedTask: Analyze the five OOP Design Practice and Review examples. Identify class responsibilities, interface, object state, lifetime and dispatch behavior where relevant.
practise.independentTask: Design a small C++ program demonstrating oop design practice and review in a practical domain. Use clear public operations, appropriate access control, and tests for expected behavior and edge cases.
hints: Start by listing responsibilities and objects.
Keep internal state protected where needed.
Initialize objects deliberately and understand lifetime.
Use inheritance only for substitutable relationships.
Test behavior through the public interface.

questions.explanation: Focused classes are easier to maintain.
Good design emphasizes clarity and ownership.
